QuestionStmt.S: The equivalent statement of "If three vertices of a triangle are represented by cube roots of unity, then the triangle is an equilateral triangle" is

Option1Stmt.S: Three vertices of a triangle are represented by cube roots of unity and the triangle is not an equilateral triangle.

Option2Stmt.S: If a triangle is an equilateral triangle then the three vertices of a triangle are represented by cube roots of unity.

Option3Stmt.S: If three vertices of triangle are not represented by cube roots of unity then the triangle is not an equilateral triangle.

Option4Stmt.S: If a triangle is not an equilateral triangle then the three vertices of the triangle can not be represented by cube roots of unity.

Solution.S:
Let $p$: Three vertices of a triangle are represented by cube roots of unity.

$q$: The triangle is an equilateral triangle.

The logical equivalent of $p \to q$ is $\sim q \to \sim p$.

Thus the equivalent statement is: "If a triangle is not an equilateral triangle, then the three vertices of the triangle cannot be represented by cube roots of unity."

This corresponds to option D.
